q:
What are the values of \( x \) and \( y \) in the matrix equation
\(\begin{pmatrix} 10 & 0 \\ 2y & 8 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2x & 0 \\ 8 & 8 \end{pmatrix}\)
?
c:
Solution:

Step 1

The two matrices are equal, so corresponding entries are equal.

\( \begin{pmatrix} 10 & 0 \\ 2y & 8 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2x & 0 \\ 8 & 8 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

By matrix equality, \( 2x = 10 \) and \( 2y = 8 \).

Therefore \( x = 5 \) and \( y = 4 \).

Final Answer:

\( x = 5,\ y = 4 \)

q:
Determine the order of
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)
and write down the entry in the first row and third column.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( A \) has 1 row and 4 columns, so it is a row matrix of order \( 1 \times 4 \).

Step 2

The entry in the first row and third column is \( 1 \).

Final Answer:

\( 1 \times 4 \), entry \( 1 \)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( A^T \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( A \) is of order \( 3 \times 2 \). The transpose \( A^T \) is the \( 2 \times 3 \) matrix whose rows are the columns of \( A \).

Step 2

\( A^T = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(A^T = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(P = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( P + Q \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

The matrices have the same order, so add corresponding entries.

\( P + Q = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} 3+1 & -2+5 \\ 1+2 & 4+3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(\begin{pmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
Write down the negative of
\(\begin{pmatrix} 5 & -8 \\ 4 & -7 \end{pmatrix}\)
.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

If \( A = (a_{ij}) \), then \( -A = (-a_{ij}) \). Change the sign of each entry.

Step 2

\( \begin{pmatrix} -5 & -(-8) \\ -4 & -(-7) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -5 & 8 \\ -4 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(\begin{pmatrix} -5 & 8 \\ -4 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( 5A \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

Multiply each entry of \( A \) by the scalar 5.

\( 5A = 5\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} 15 & 10 \\ 5 & 20 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(\begin{pmatrix} 15 & 10 \\ 5 & 20 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( (-1)A \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( (-1)A = (-1)\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} -3 & -2 \\ -1 & -4 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(\begin{pmatrix} -3 & -2 \\ -1 & -4 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
Given that
\(O = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\)
, show that \( O + A = A \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( O + A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} = A \)


Step 2

The zero matrix is the identity element for addition of matrices.

Final Answer:

\( O + A = A \)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( A - B \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( A - B = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} 4-2 & 1-5 \\ -2-0 & 3-1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ -2 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(\begin{pmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ -2 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
Let
\(P = \begin{pmatrix} x & 5 \\ -3 & y \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(Q = \begin{pmatrix} 9 & -3 \\ 5 & -7 \end{pmatrix}\)
. Find \( x \) and \( y \) given that \( P = Q^T \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

The transpose of \( Q \) is obtained by writing rows as columns.

\( Q^T = \begin{pmatrix} 9 & 5 \\ -3 & -7 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

By matrix equality, \( P = Q^T \) gives \( x = 9 \) and \( y = -7 \).

Final Answer:

\( x = 9,\ y = -7 \)

q:
If
\(B = \begin{pmatrix} -3 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ -4 & 1 & 5 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( (B^T)^T \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( B \) is \( 2 \times 4 \), so \( B^T \) is \( 4 \times 2 \). Transposing again returns the original matrix.

Step 2

\( (B^T)^T = B = \begin{pmatrix} -3 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ -4 & 1 & 5 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\( (B^T)^T = B \)

q: If \( A \) is of order \( 1 \times 2 \) and \( B \) is of order \( 2 \times 2 \), which of the products \( AB \) and \( BA \) is possible? State the order of any product that exists.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

Order of \( A \) is \( 1 \times 2 \) and order of \( B \) is \( 2 \times 2 \). The inner numbers 2 and 2 are the same, so \( AB \) exists and has order \( 1 \times 2 \).

Step 2

Order of \( B \) is \( 2 \times 2 \) and order of \( A \) is \( 1 \times 2 \). The inner numbers 2 and 1 are different, so \( BA \) does not exist.

Final Answer:

\( AB \) exists and is \( 1 \times 2 \); \( BA \) does not exist.

q:
Evaluate
\((2\ {-3}\ 4)\begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}\)
.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

Multiply each entry of the row matrix by the corresponding entry of the column matrix and add.

\( (2)(5) + (-3)(1) + (4)(2) \)


Step 2

\( = 10 - 3 + 8 = 15 \)


Final Answer:

\( (15) \)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( \det A \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

For
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\)
, \( \det A = ad - bc \).

Step 2

\( \det A = (3)(4) - (5)(2) = 12 - 10 = 2 \)


Final Answer:

\( 2 \)

q:
Find, if it exists, the inverse of
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\)
.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( \det A = (3)(2) - (1)(5) = 6 - 5 = 1 \ne 0 \)
, so \( A^{-1} \) exists.

Step 2

Then
\(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\det A}\begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -5 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -5 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)
.

Final Answer:

\(A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -5 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
Find \( \det N \) if
\(N = \begin{pmatrix} 6 & 3 \\ -4 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\)
and state whether \( N^{-1} \) exists.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( \det N = (6)(-2) - (3)(-4) = -12 + 12 = 0 \)


Step 2

Since \( \det N = 0 \), \( N \) is singular and \( N^{-1} \) does not exist.

Final Answer:

\( \det N = 0 \); \( N^{-1} \) does not exist.

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 5 \\ 6 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(I = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( AI \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( AI = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 5 \\ 6 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7+0 & 0+5 \\ 6+0 & 0+4 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 5 \\ 6 & 4 \end{pmatrix} = A \)


Final Answer:

\(AI = A = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 5 \\ 6 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(B = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( AB \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( A \) is \( 1 \times 3 \) and \( B \) is \( 3 \times 1 \), so \( AB \) is \( 1 \times 1 \).

Step 2

\( AB = (1)(4) + (2)(0) + (3)(1) = 4 + 0 + 3 = (7) \)


Final Answer:

\( (7) \)

q:
Find the matrix \( A \) which satisfies
\(A + \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}\)
.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

Add the negative of
\(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
to both sides.

\( A = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} -7 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(A = \begin{pmatrix} -7 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
Solve
\(X + \begin{pmatrix} -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 5 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\)
for the \( 2 \times 2 \) matrix \( X \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

Add the negative of
\(\begin{pmatrix} -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\)
to both sides.

Step 2

\( X = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 5 & 4 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & -2 \\ 5 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(X = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & -2 \\ 5 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 9 & 12 \\ 6 & 9 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( \dfrac{1}{3}A \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

Multiply each entry by \( \dfrac{1}{3} \).

\( \dfrac{1}{3}A = \begin{pmatrix} \frac{9}{3} & \frac{12}{3} \\ \frac{6}{3} & \frac{9}{3} \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \)


Final Answer:

\(\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(B = \begin{pmatrix} -2 & -3 \\ -4 & -5 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( A + B \) and hence name the relationship between \( A \) and \( B \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} -2 & -3 \\ -4 & -5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = O \)


Step 2

Hence \( B \) is the negative of \( A \), written \( B = -A \).

Final Answer:

\( A + B = O \), so \( B = -A \)

q:

.
c:

\( (2)(2) + (3)(1) \)


Step 2

Final Answer:

\( (7) \)

q:

c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( \det A = (1)(1) - (2)(0) = 1 \ne 0 \)
, so the inverse exists.

Step 2

\(A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
.

Final Answer:

\(A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
and
\(B = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( IB \).
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( IB = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 7 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4+0 & 5+0 \\ 0+6 & 0+7 \end{pmatrix} \)


Step 2

\( = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 7 \end{pmatrix} = B \)


Final Answer:

\( IB = B \)

q:

q:
If
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
, find \( \det A \) and state whether \( A \) is singular or non-singular.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

\( \det A = (4)(1) - (2)(2) = 4 - 4 = 0 \)


Step 2

Since \( \det A = 0 \), \( A \) is singular.

Final Answer:

\( \det A = 0 \); singular.

c:

q:
Find \( x \) and \( y \) if
\(\begin{pmatrix} 3x & -y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 12 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\)
.
c:
Solution:

Step 1

The matrices have the same order \( 1 \times 2 \). By matrix equality, corresponding entries are equal.

Step 2

\(3x = 12\)
\(\implies x = 4\)


\(-y = 0\)
\(\implies y = 0\)


Final Answer:

\( x = 4,\ y = 0 \)
